dataSources: `index=edge-hub-health` sourcetype=edge_hub cpu_percent, memory_percent, disk_used_mb Collected via Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
app: Splunk Edge Hub (system monitoring), Splunk OT Intelligence — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)
spl:
index=edge-hub-health sourcetype=edge_hub
| bin _time span=1h
| stats avg(cpu_percent) as avg_cpu, max(cpu_percent) as peak_cpu,
        avg(memory_percent) as avg_mem, max(memory_percent) as peak_mem,
        latest(disk_used_mb) as disk_used by host, _time
| eval cpu_headroom=(100 - peak_cpu), mem_headroom=(100 - peak_mem), disk_available_mb=(32000 - disk_used)
| where cpu_headroom < 10 OR mem_headroom < 5 OR disk_available_mb < 1000
| eval resource_alert="CAPACITY_WARNING"
description: Prevents Edge Hub performance degradation and data loss by tracking resource utilization and planning for container resource allocation.
value: Early 'Edge Hub Resource Capacity Planning & CPU/Memory Utilization' detection reduces operational risk and delayed incident response by giving Operations operators a Splunk-native signal before manual triage or audit channels surface the issue.
implementation: Edge Hub OS reports CPU %, memory %, disk %, and container-level resource stats to edge-hub-health index every 5 minutes. NXP IMX8M has 8GB RAM total: allocate 4GB for OS/system, 4GB for containers. Each container configured with memory limits in edge.json (e.g., 512MB, 256MB). Monitor peak CPU during data bursts (e.g., video processing, FFT computation). Alert when peak CPU > 80% (insufficient headroom for spikes) or memory > 95% (OOM risk). Plan container consolidation or upgrade if resources consistently constrained.
visualization: CPU usage trend, memory usage gauge, container resource breakdown pie, capacity projection.

4. **Onboarding burst** — New entities produce atypical volume until baseline stabilizes.

detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Install and configure the required add-on or app: Splunk Edge Hub (system monitoring), Splunk OT Intelligence.
• Ensure the following data sources are available: `index=edge-hub-health` sourcetype=edge_hub cpu_percent, memory_percent, disk_used_mb.
• For app installation, inputs.conf, and Splunk directory layout, see the Implementation guide: docs/implementation-guide.md

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Edge Hub OS reports CPU %, memory %, disk %, and container-level resource stats to edge-hub-health index every 5 minutes. NXP IMX8M has 8GB RAM total: allocate 4GB for OS/system, 4GB for containers. Each container configured with memory limits in edge.json (e.g., 512MB, 256MB). Monitor peak CPU during data bursts (e.g., video processing, FFT computation). Alert when peak CPU > 80% (insufficient headroom for spikes) or memory > 95% (OOM risk). Plan container consolidation or upgrade if resources …

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following SPL in Search (then save as report or alert; adjust time range and threshold as needed):

```spl
index=edge-hub-health sourcetype=edge_hub
| bin _time span=1h
| stats avg(cpu_percent) as avg_cpu, max(cpu_percent) as peak_cpu,
        avg(memory_percent) as avg_mem, max(memory_percent) as peak_mem,
        latest(disk_used_mb) as disk_used by host, _time
| eval cpu_headroom=(100 - peak_cpu), mem_headroom=(100 - peak_mem), disk_available_mb=(32000 - disk_used)
| where cpu_headroom < 10 OR mem_headroom < 5 OR disk_available_mb < 1000
| eval resource_alert="CAPACITY_WARNING"
```

Understanding this SPL

**Edge Hub Resource Capacity Planning & CPU/Memory Utilization** — Prevents Edge Hub performance degradation and data loss by tracking resource utilization and planning for container resource allocation.

Documented **Data sources**: `index=edge-hub-health` sourcetype=edge_hub cpu_percent, memory_percent, disk_used_mb. **App/TA** (typical add-on context): Splunk Edge Hub (system monitoring), Splunk OT Intelligence. The SPL below should target the same indexes and sourcetypes you configured for that feed—rename `index=` / `sourcetype=` if your deployment differs.

The first pipeline stage scopes events using **index**: edge-hub-health; **sourcetype**: edge_hub. That sourcetype matches what this use case lists under Data sources.

**Pipeline walkthrough**

• Scopes the data: index=edge-hub-health, sourcetype=edge_hub. Cross-check against **Data sources** above so indexes and sourcetypes match your ingestion.
• Discretizes time or numeric ranges with `bin`/`bucket`.
• `stats` rolls up events into metrics; results are split **by host, _time** so each row reflects one combination of those dimensions.
• `eval` defines or adjusts **cpu_headroom** — often to normalize units, derive a ratio, or prepare for thresholds.
• Filters the current rows with `where cpu_headroom < 10 OR mem_headroom < 5 OR disk_available_mb < 1000` — typically the threshold or rule expression for this monitoring goal.
• `eval` defines or adjusts **resource_alert** — often to normalize units, derive a ratio, or prepare for thresholds.


Step 3 — Validate
Confirm metric or event volume in the time range, then compare trends and device status to the Splunk Edge Hub admin UI or the mobile app for the same devices. Verify metric names, hosts, and time skew.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Add the search to a dashboard or set up alert actions (email, webhook, PagerDuty, etc.) as required. Document the use case in your runbook and assign an owner. Consider visualizations: CPU usage trend, memory usage gauge, container resource breakdown pie, capacity projection.
